tonight.headline: 0–4 in all but name: McMillan scored 45
body: Bad news first. You trail 97.6 to 153.6 with only Alvin Kamara left, and ESPN gives you 1%. Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday night, 45.2 points, in the game your Jalen Coker missed. Add Kyren Williams' 36.7 and Aye-Aye had the week's best score before your bench came into it.

Your bench did come into it: Monangai 28.0 and Gordon 18.0 sat behind Tuten's 11.1. That is 34.9 points before Kamara plays, and it wouldn't have been enough. Nothing can be changed tonight. Monday's news is that Monangai's thumb is day-to-day, which is good for your backfield and closes the seat a receiver claim was waiting on. Tomorrow's brief is the last before claims process.

case.label: Their side
case.body: McMillan 45.2, Kyren Williams 36.7 in the flex, McCaffrey 16.0, St. Brown 15.5. They are finished at 153.56 and left Aaron Jones' 16.8 on the bench.

case.label: Your side
case.body: Allen 18.5, Fairbairn 16, Warren 15.6, Likely 13.6, Tuten 11.1, Addison 9.1, the Vikings 8, Wilson 5.7. Three receivers inactive. No starter was hurt.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. Kamara would need 56 points. He is expected to play; the Saints' inactive list wasn't readable by 16:57.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN league file · Week 4 archive · CBS Sports

whatWentWrong.title: The thumb is fine, so the seat you were waiting on stays shut
whatWentWrong.lead: Monangai is day-to-day and his coach expects him to be OK. That is good for the roster and it removes this morning's likeliest drop for a receiver claim.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: He had imaging on his right thumb on Monday. Ben Johnson: 'We think he's going to be OK... more of a day-to-day type deal' (Chicago Sun-Times; A to Z Sports, 5 Oct). No result was published. He ran 30 times for 146 and two touchdowns on Sunday (archive). Caleb Williams is out for Week 5 and Bagent starts at Green Bay.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: There is still no Do-first card, for a different reason from this morning. Then the drop was unknown; now it is narrowed to one seat. Wilson, Warren, Kamara, Gordon and Addison each have an injured teammate, Monangai and Gordon just scored 28 and 18, and Jefferson and McLaurin have bigger roles waiting. That leaves Coker: hurt, on bye, no return date, and 87% rostered. Whether Metcalf is worth his seat depends on Jefferson. Waiting costs nothing, because claims don't process until Wed 01:00 Mexico City and tomorrow's brief comes first.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson ruled out for New Orleans on Tuesday: then a healthy receiver is worth more than Coker's two idle weeks, and tomorrow's brief says so with the card.

whatWentWrong.sources: Week 1–4 archive · Chicago Sun-Times · A to Z Sports · CBS Sports · Yahoo

whatWentWrong.title: No word on Jefferson in either direction
whatWentWrong.lead: This morning his coach had no projection for Week 5. By late afternoon nobody had added to it, and the bye is Week 6.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: O'Connell: 'I don't have any real projection on whether we'll have him or not' (Yahoo, 5 Oct). His Monday press conference dealt with the offensive line instead: left guard Donovan Jackson's season is probably over and Darrisaw is in the concussion protocol (Vikings.com). McLaurin has no update either; Yahoo lists him 'TBD'. Coker has no return date.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Week 5's receivers are Wilson and Addison, with a back in the flex and three backs to choose from. That is a lineup, so a third receiver is depth and not a need. It is why the claim is tomorrow's question and not tonight's.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A report on Tuesday that Jefferson will sit through the bye. Wednesday's practice report comes after claims process, so Tuesday's reporting is all the claim will have.

case.body: 5 targets, after 8, 5, 10 (archive), from Malik Willis, who was 9 of 17 for 85. A share of very little is very little, and Miami are off in Week 6.

case.body: Eight or more targets against Cincinnati, or a different quarterback in Miami.

doNotChase.lead: Six targets with Smith out, in an offence that threw for 93 yards.

case.body: DeVonta Smith is expected to miss multiple games (Garafolo via the Inquirer, 5 Oct). Yahoo calls Lemon an 'upside rookie stash'.
